title: Connections, Questions & Making Plans
subtitle: B1 practice with relationships, subject and object questions, friendly suggestions and arrangements.
lessonNotes: Use subject questions to ask who or what does an action.
Use object questions to ask who or what receives an action.
Use should, could, Why don't we and How about for friendly suggestions.
Use clear time and place phrases to arrange a meeting.

grammar.title: Subject and object questions
grammar.rule: Ask accurately about the person who does an action and the person who receives it.

grammar.title: Suggestions and arrangements
grammar.rule: Offer friendly ideas and agree a time, place and alternative plan.
examples: Why don't we meet at six?
How about meeting at the library?

vocabulary.example: My colleague helped me prepare for the meeting.
They keep in touch by sending messages.

vocabulary.meaning: to trust or depend on someone
vocabulary.example: You can rely on her when you need help.

vocabulary.meaning: to travel around a place and learn about it
vocabulary.example: We could explore the old town.

practice.why: Subject questions do not need did.

reading.title: A Welcome Committee
reading.text: A new resident joins a neighbourhood group, meets friendly people and makes a plan to explore the local area.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
opt: Making connections in a new place
questions.a: Making connections in a new place
questions.why: The text focuses on meeting people and making a plan.

listening.title: Making arrangements
listening.instructions: Use the linked listening activities to practise clear, everyday plans.
listening.script: External listening tasks are linked in the interactive homework.

opt: Sorry, I'm busy. Could we meet later?
questions.a: Sorry, I'm busy. Could we meet later?
